task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

**What I found:**

Your number is **555-123-2002** (Account C1001, John Smith). I've done some troubleshooting on line **L1002**:

1. **Roaming was OFF** — Since you're abroad in France, you had no roaming enabled on your line. **I've now enabled international roaming** on 555-123-2002 at no cost. ✅

2. **Your data allowance is used up** — You've used **15.1 GB out of 15.0 GB** on your Premium Plan this cycle. This is the other cause of your slow/non-working data. ✅ (resolved below, or see options)

**One more thing to check on your end:**
Since you're abroad, please make sure **Data Roaming is toggled ON in your phone's settings** — this is a separate switch from the line-level roaming I just enabled. On most phones it's under: *Settings → Connections/Network → Mobile Networks → Data Roaming*.

**About the data limit:**
Your current billing cycle ends **2025-02-28** (just a few days away). To get data working again right now, you have two options:

- **A) Refuel data (up to 2 GB)** at **$2.00/GB** on your Premium Plan — so 1 GB = $2.00, 2 GB = $4.00, added to your bill. This would cover you for the next few days until the cycle resets.
- **B) Do nothing and wait** — your data resets when the new cycle starts.

Would you like me to refuel data for you, and if so, how many GB (1 or 2, up to the 2 GB max)?

Data refueled successfully ✅ — **2 GB added** to line 555-123-2002 for **$4.00** (added to your bill). Your available data for the rest of this cycle is now 2 GB.

Now, to your questions — and I found a couple more things to fix:

## 1. Data Roaming — YES, please turn it ON ✅
Since you're in France and outside our home network, this needs to be on. Go to:
**Settings → Connections (or Network & Internet) → Mobile Networks → Data Roaming → ON**

This is safe — I've already enabled roaming on your line at no cost, so there are no roaming charges for enabling the service itself.

## 2. Data Saver — YES, please turn it OFF ✅
Data Saver restricts background data usage and can make apps and browsing crawl. Go to:
**Settings → Connections → Data Usage → Data Saver → OFF**

## 3. You're stuck on 2G — please change your network mode ⚠️
This is very likely your biggest speed culprit. 2G is an old technology that can't deliver usable data — and it also **won't send or receive picture/video (MMS) messages**. Please switch it:
**Settings → Connections → Mobile Networks → Network Mode → select "5G/4G preferred" (or "LTE/4G preferred")**

## 4. Poor signal
The 2G lock and poor signal often go hand in hand — switching to 4G/5G should help. If your signal is still poor after that, try moving near a window or going outside, as indoor coverage abroad can be weak.

## Please do this after making the changes:
**Restart (reboot) your phone.** This lets all the new settings — especially the network mode and roaming — fully take effect.

## Summary of what we've done today:
| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Roaming enabled on line 555-123-2002 | ✅ Done (no cost) |
| Data refueled +2 GB | ✅ Done ($4.00 on your bill) |
| Data Roaming ON on your phone | ⬜ You to do |
| Data Saver OFF | ⬜ You to do |
| Network mode → 4G/5G preferred | ⬜ You to do |
| Reboot phone | ⬜ You to do |

Once you've made those changes and rebooted, let me know how the data is working. If it's still slow or not connecting, I'll dig further with you. Also, a quick reminder: your billing cycle ends **2025-02-28**, so your 15 GB allowance resets then.

turns.thought:
Good progress — you now have a working data connection at **27.50 Mbps ("Good")**, up from dropping out or crawling. But I hear you, and there are a couple of things I want to confirm before we call it done.

**First — two things I need you to check, because they're the biggest speed levers:**

1. **Network mode — did you switch off 2G?** Your last status bar showed **2G**, and 2G simply can't deliver fast data. Please go to *Settings → Connections → Mobile Networks → Network Mode* and select **"5G/4G preferred"** (or "LTE/4G"). If you haven't done this yet, this alone could be holding you at "Good."

2. **Data Saver — is it OFF now?** While it's ON, it actively restricts data usage and will keep your speed suppressed. Please confirm it's turned off.

After both are set, **restart your phone** and re-run the speed test. Also check your status bar — it should now show **4G/LTE or 5G** rather than 2G. If it's still showing 2G, tell me.

**On the VPN:** Our troubleshooting guide does list an active VPN as a possible cause of reduced speeds. However, the step to disconnect it applies when performance comes back as **"Poor"** — yours came back **"Good"**, so I'm not going to instruct you to turn it off. It's entirely your call, and since you're abroad and may be relying on it for work or privacy, I'd weigh that carefully. If you do want to test it, you can disconnect it temporarily, re-run the speed test, and reconnect afterward.

**On reaching "Excellent" — let me be upfront with you.** The speed-related steps available to me are: airplane mode, SIM status, mobile data enabled, roaming (line + device), Data Saver, VPN, network mode, and your data limit. We've now worked through all of them — and your data limit, which was the other hard cap, is resolved with the 2 GB refuel.

So please confirm the network mode and Data Saver changes are in place and re-test. If you're still not at "Excellent" after that, say the word and I'll transfer you to a human agent who has additional network optimization options I don't have access to.
